object_description: school volume set directly above an underground triple gymnasium, linked by a stretched concrete roof
geometry_property: school stacked above a buried gymnasium
set back at the rear building edge
height well below the neighbouring eaves
design_condition: the triple gymnasium goes underground and the school is placed directly above it at the rear building edge between the two historic wings, with a stretched concrete roof spanning between the old buildings as a covered break area

positive: Putting the gymnasium underground and stacking the school above it favours the outdoor space
An ensemble of three independent buildings is created
The new building fits very naturally and with the necessary restraint thanks to its set-back position
Its height development stays significantly below the eaves of the neighbouring historic building
The compactness of the above-ground volume is successful
The new roof element is seen as a central entrance and meeting place
A specific static concept develops from stacking gymnasium and school
Floor-to-ceiling concrete slabs span the gymnasium and form a kind of roof structure with the outer walls
This creates space and generates the three large ground floor rooms
Three light showcases promise transparency and visibility, guaranteeing spatial references at ground level
The layout of the classroom floor is convincing
The sports area is impressively developed both operationally and spatially
The underground gymnasium is illuminated via six room-forming light showcases
The viewing gallery reachable independently of the entrance hall benefits directly from the light
It gives access to all cloakrooms and forms an attractive connection to the existing building
The relief of the two-storey concrete supports can be related to the ornamentation of the historic building
The project proves economically and ecologically sound and achieves the desired energy standard
A carefully developed project that is a valuable urban contribution and works well operationally
negative: The expressive roof form, tapered edges and closed entrance volumes create a competing massiveness
The roof therefore has more of a separating than a connecting effect
The strongly structurally determined room division appears inflexible
The staircase to the upper floors seems complicated and hidden
The strong distinction between massive base and delicate superstructure is incomprehensible
It weakens the presence of the new building in the ensemble
The glass lintel and parapet areas seem out of place and recall 1960s office architecture
The project is not entirely convincing in its architectural implementation
